class.name: MultiMeshBody3D
class.brief_description: Collision for each instance of a [MultiMesh].
class.description: A [MultiMeshInstance3D] draws thousands of objects cheaply, but nothing can bump into them. MultiMeshBody3D gives each instance a [member shape], placed by its transform, so scattered props (bollards, benches, rocks) are solid too. Put it where the [MultiMeshInstance3D] is (as its child, say) with the same [member multimesh]: [codeblock] var body := MultiMeshBody3D.new() body.multimesh = $Bollards.multimesh body.shape = preload("res://props/bollard_shape.tres") $Bollards.add_child(body) [/codeblock] The shapes are made a few dozen at a time over frames. Every MultiMeshBody3D shares one queue and one budget a frame, [code]physics/3d/multimesh_collision_budget_ms[/code] (spread with [FrameBudget]), working on the one nearest the camera first and its nearest instances first: a streamed world's props never hold up a frame, and what's ahead of the player is solid before what's far off. Raycasts and contacts report this node as the collider; [method get_instance] says which instance was hit. Switched off with [member Node.process_mode], it leaves the physics world, as a [CollisionObject3D] does. The instances' transforms are read from the [MultiMesh] once, when the shapes are made: call [method rebuild] after moving its instances. A [MultiMesh] with no mesh keeps its [member MultiMesh.buffer] when it's set whole, and is read at once. One with a mesh is read back from the renderer, which waits for the GPU to finish the frames in flight: for collision added while the game runs (a streamed world's), give the body a [MultiMesh] of its own with no mesh, its buffer set whole. Headless, Godot's stand-in renderer keeps a [MultiMesh]'s transforms only when its [member MultiMesh.buffer] is set whole, as a loaded one's is.
